Documentation Index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.perplexity.ai/llms.txt
Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
Agent API Models
Compare Agent API models, token pricing, supported service tiers, and provider documentation.
[!NOTE]
Looking for ranked web results instead of a generated answer? Use the Search API at POST /search. It takes no model parameter and bills per successful request, not per token. Start with the Search API quickstart (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/quickstart.md).
Available Models
The Agent API provides a unified interface to models from multiple providers with transparent token-based pricing.
Pricing rates are published per model and may differ from provider list prices. All charges are based on actual token consumption, and every API response includes exact token counts so you know your costs per request.
The Service tiers column lists optional non-default tiers. An em dash means the model uses default processing only.
A rate with a context-length range, such as (≤272k), changes when the input is above that range. A single value applies at every context length.
Cache write is the rate for input tokens written to the prompt cache, billed instead of the input rate for those tokens. Where a table has no Cache write column or shows an em dash, written tokens bill at the input rate. See Prompt Caching (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/prompt-caching.md) to control what is written.
[!TIP]
Looking for pre-configured model setups? See Effort Levels (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/effort.md) — optimized for specific use cases.
[tab] Anthropic
[card] Anthropic
Claude Opus (highest reasoning), Sonnet (balanced), and Haiku (fastest, cheapest).
[!NOTE]
max_output_tokens is optional for all models, including Anthropic models. When omitted, each generation can produce up to 128,000 output tokens, capped by the model's supported limit. Set it to impose a total output-token budget across the run. An effort level or saved profile with an explicit budget still supplies that budget.
Claude Fable 5.2 requires non-Zero Data Retention (non-ZDR) model access. Contact api@perplexity.ai (mailto:api@perplexity.ai) to request access.
[tab] OpenAI
[card] OpenAI
OpenAI GPT models.
For GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra, the calculator below estimates input and output costs, treating all input tokens as uncached. For tokens read from or written to the cache, use the corresponding cache rate in the table instead of the input rate.
[tab] Google
[card] Google
Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and Gemini 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash.
Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon rates are introductory pricing through November 30, 2026. The google/gemini-3.8-flash and google/gemini-3.7-flash rates apply through December 31, 2026. Reasoning tokens are billed at the output-token rate.
[tab] xAI
[card] xAI
Grok 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5.
[tab] Z.AI
[card] Z.AI
GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash — Z.AI reasoning models.
[tab] DeepSeek
[card] DeepSeek
DeepSeek V4 Pro, an open-weight reasoning model.
[tab] Moonshot AI
[card] Moonshot AI
Kimi K3 — Moonshot AI's flagship reasoning model.
[!NOTE]
Kimi K3 accepts minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max reasoning effort. minimal uses low effort, while xhigh and max use maximum effort. Reasoning tokens are billed at the output-token rate.
[tab] NVIDIA
[card] NVIDIA
Nemotron 3.5 Super is a reasoning model with a 1,048,576-token context window and up to 131,072 output tokens. It accepts text input only.
[tab] Perplexity
[card] Perplexity
Perplexity's grounded search model.
Service tiers
Omit service_tier, or set it to auto or default, to use default processing. flex uses lower-cost, best-effort capacity at 0.5× the listed token prices. priority uses higher-priority processing at 2× the listed token prices. fast is accepted as an alias for priority. These multipliers apply only to models that list the tier in the Service tiers column. Other models always bill at the listed rate.
When you provide model or models, the Agent API applies flex or priority only if the selected model—or every model in a fallback list—supports that tier. An unsupported tier does not cause the request to be rejected; the API ignores service_tier and uses default processing. Requests that specify only an effort level or profile retain the tier until the model is resolved. The response's service_tier field reports the tier that served the request.
[!WARNING]
Not all third-party models support all features (e.g., reasoning, tools). Check model documentation for specific capabilities.
Using a Model
[accordion] Response
[!TIP]
See Your Costs in Real-Time: Every response includes a usage field with exact input tokens, output tokens, and cache read tokens. Calculate your cost instantly using the pricing table above.
Model Fallback
For high-availability applications, you can specify multiple models in a fallback chain. When one model fails or is unavailable, the API automatically tries the next model in the chain.
[card] Model Fallback Chain (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/model-fallback.md)
Learn how to use model fallback chains to ensure high availability and reliability by automatically trying multiple models when one fails.
[!NOTE]
Example:
For detailed examples, pricing information, and best practices, see the Model Fallback documentation (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/model-fallback.md).
Next Steps
[card] Web Search (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/web-search.md)
Equip your model with web search for source-grounded context.
[card] Prompt Guide (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/prompt-guide.md)
Write prompts that get the most out of the Agent API.
[card] Output Control (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/output-control.md)
Shape responses with structured outputs and JSON schemas.
[card] Finance Search (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/tools/finance-search.md)
Query market data, filings, and ticker-level information.

Documentation Index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.perplexity.ai/llms.txt
Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
Pricing
Understand Perplexity API pricing, model rates, request fees, billing setup, and rate-limit references.
Each Perplexity API bills differently. The rates are in the sections below.
* Orchestrator API: per token, at each model's rates. The service tier (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md#billing) can change token rates on supported OpenAI models. No per-request fees. Requests rejected with a 429 are not billed.
* Agent API: per token, at each model's rates, plus tool fees. Most tools bill per call; sandbox bills per started 20-minute block of container time, plus each SDK web search made inside it. The flex (0.5×) and priority (2×) service tiers change the token rates only for models that list that tier on the Agent API Models page (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/models.md). Other models always bill at the listed rate.
* Search API: per successful request.
* Monitor API: per succeeded Search run or counted fetched Page URL from a succeeded run. Perplexity bills Agent runs as Agent API usage (#agent-api-pricing).
* Context API: per URL returned with status ok or not_modified. With criteria, scoring tokens bill as Decisions API input tokens.
* Embeddings API: per token.
* Decisions API: per input token, including fetched page text and search evidence. Output tokens are free. Web grounding (#web-grounding) adds fees for web searches and URL fetches.
For billing setup, payment methods, and usage monitoring, see the Admin section (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/projects.md). For rate limits, see Rate Limits & Usage Tiers (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/admin/rate-limits-usage-tiers.md).
Orchestrator API Pricing
Orchestrator API usage is billed per token at each model's published rates, with no per-request fees. Every model has its own input and output rate, with cache reads billed at the model's cache-read rate and reasoning tokens billed at the output rate. Some models also charge for cache writes; see Orchestrator billing (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md#billing). You are billed at the requested model's rates regardless of which deployment serves the request; with perplexity/auto, at the rates of the model that served it.
See Orchestrator Models & Pricing (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md) for the full per-model rate card, including cache-read rates and usage tiers.
For supported OpenAI models, service tiers (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/models.md#billing) scale token rates by 0.5× for flex and 2× for priority. The listed rates for google/gemini-3.7-flash and google/gemini-3.8-flash apply through December 31, 2026.
Agent API Pricing
The Agent API charges for model tokens and tool calls. The catalog includes models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Z.AI, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, NVIDIA, and Perplexity.
Model Pricing
See the Agent API Models page (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/models.md) for input, output, and cache-read rates. For models that charge for cache writes, see Prompt Caching (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/prompt-caching.md).
The introductory rates for google/gemini-4-argon and google/gemini-4-carbon apply through November 30, 2026. The listed rates for google/gemini-3.7-flash and google/gemini-3.8-flash apply through December 31, 2026.
Tool Pricing
When using tools with the Agent API:
[!NOTE]
Most tool costs are per invocation. sandbox is billed per started 20-minute block of container time, plus each SDK web search made inside it. Tool costs are separate from model token costs.
Search API Pricing
[!NOTE]
Billing unit: Search API charges for each successful POST /search request, not for each query in the request. A successful request containing an array of up to five queries is one billing unit. Invalid requests, rate-limited requests, and upstream failures are not billed. A successful response is billed even when it returns no results. There are no additional token-based charges.
Search API cost = successful requests ÷ 1,000 × the price per 1K requests.
What a result contains, the request controls, and the limits on queries and results are in How Search Works (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/overview.md).
Monitor API Pricing
Search and Page cost = (succeeded Search runs + counted fetched URLs from succeeded Page runs) × $0.001. Failed and skipped Search and Page runs are free.
A succeeded Search run is billed once, even if it performs multiple searches or returns no findings.
In the calculator (#estimate-your-cost), choose Monitor API to estimate Search and Page costs. Enter both totals for the same period. The run's usage.cost reports list-price cost, not the invoice or amount charged.
Rate limits
See Monitor API limits (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/admin/rate-limits-usage-tiers.md#monitor-api-limits) for HTTP request limits by usage tier.
Context API Pricing
The Context API (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/context/quickstart.md) returns the content of web pages you already have URLs for. It costs $1.00 per 1,000 fetched URLs ($0.001 per URL). Requests without criteria have no token billing.
[!NOTE]
Billing unit: each URL in a successful POST /v1/context response whose status.type is ok or not_modified, whatever formats asks for. Highlights and metadata-only requests with "formats": [] are billed the same way. URLs that fail are free, including invalid, blocked, empty, and timed-out URLs.
Context API cost without criteria = billable URLs (ok or not_modified) ÷ 1,000 × $1.00.
With criteria (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/context/criteria), scoring is billed as Decisions API input tokens (#decisions-api-pricing) on top of the per-URL price: the page text plus your questions, for each scored page. The response reports the count as usage.criteria.input_tokens.
To estimate your cost, open the calculator (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md?calc=context#estimate-your-cost) and enter the URLs you expect to fetch per month.
Each successful response reports the billed URL count in usage.fetched_urls and its list-price cost in usage.cost.total_cost, before any account-specific discounts, credits, or adjustments.
Embeddings API Pricing
Generate high-quality text embeddings for semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and other machine learning applications.
Contextualized Embeddings v2
Text inputs use the token price. Image inputs use the image price.
Standard Embeddings
Contextualized Embeddings
Embeddings cost = tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × the model's rate. For example, 40M tokens on pplx-embed-context-v1-4b cost 40 × $0.05 = $2.00.
To use the Embeddings API, see the Embeddings quickstart (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/embeddings/quickstart.md).
Decisions API Pricing
The Decisions API answers yes/no, multiple-choice, and scored questions about text and images with calibrated probabilities, and finds matching text spans with locate questions.
[!NOTE]
Aliases: pplx-decider-latest and perplexity/pplx-decider-latest select pplx-decider-v1.3. pplx-decider-flash-latest and perplexity/pplx-decider-flash-latest select pplx-decider-flash-v1.3. An alias bills at the rate of the model it selects. pplx-decider-v1.1-27b is a legacy alias of pplx-decider-v1-27b; both bill at $0.02.
Billing unit: you pay for input tokens, plus web searches and URL fetches if you set mode: "web_grounding". The state, every question, any images, fetched page text, and any search results added to the state count as input; the response reports the exact number as usage.input_tokens, so you can compute the token cost of a request from the response you already receive. A request with 600 input tokens costs $0.000012 on pplx-decider-v1.3 or pplx-decider-v1.2 and $0.000006 on pplx-decider-flash-v1.3 or pplx-decider-flash-v1.2.
Web grounding
A request with mode: "web_grounding" runs one Fast Search (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/search/fast-search.md) for each of its questions, up to 100, before the model answers. Each search costs $0.001 ($1 per 1,000), in addition to input tokens, so at most $0.10 in searches per request. Questions that produce the same search query share one search.
When state is a page URL, the API also fetches the page before searching. Each successful URL fetch costs $0.0005; a failed fetch is not billed. One successful fetch and three successful searches cost $0.0035, plus input tokens.
* Billed: every search that returns, even with no results. Completed searches and successful URL fetches remain billable if the request later fails, for example because the input exceeds the token limit.
* Not billed: a search that fails or runs out of time, a question with no text to search, and requests rejected before search: an invalid mode, more than 100 questions, a missing or unknown model, or a state that is not a string, object, or array. A request can be billed for fewer searches than it has questions.
* Input tokens: fetched page text and search evidence are billed as input tokens and included in usage.input_tokens.
See Web grounding (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/decisions/decisions.md#web-grounding).
To use the Decisions API, see the Decisions quickstart (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/decisions/quickstart.md).
Token counts: 1 token is about 4 characters of English text. The exact count varies with language and content.
Cost Examples
To estimate an Agent API request, calculate these costs for each model call:
* Fresh input tokens × the model's input rate ÷ 1,000,000.
* Cache reads × the model's cache-read rate ÷ 1,000,000.
* Cache writes × the model's cache-write rate ÷ 1,000,000, if the model charges for writes. Otherwise, use the model's input rate for those tokens.
* Output tokens × the model's output rate ÷ 1,000,000. Output tokens already include reasoning tokens.
Use the model rate (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/models.md) for the full input size of each call. On supported models, multiply token costs by 0.5 for flex or 2 for priority. Add each applicable tool fee (#tool-pricing) once. Service tiers do not change tool fees.
Actual effort level costs vary with the model, token usage, and tool calls. When present, usage.cost.total_cost reports an estimate. Check Billing in the API Console for charged amounts.
Purchase Options
* Perplexity API Platform on AWS Marketplace (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/resources/aws-marketplace.md): buy API credits through AWS Marketplace with consolidated billing and enterprise procurement.
* Contact the sales team (https://perplexity.typeform.com/to/m3WnMaG6): ask about custom pricing, dedicated support, and enterprise features.

billing.text:
Documentation Index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.perplexity.ai/llms.txt
Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
Orchestrator Models & Pricing
Orchestrator API models with context windows, output limits, per-token pricing, and usage tier requirements.
Available Models
Every model below uses the same prefixed ID, such as openai/gpt-6-luna or perplexity/glm-5.3, in Chat Completions (https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/gateway-chat-completions-post.md), Responses (https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/gateway-responses-post.md), and Messages (https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/gateway-messages-post.md). perplexity/auto is not a model in the tables: it picks one of these models for each request, and you are billed at that model's rate. See Routing & Reliability (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/routing-and-reliability.md).
Context window and max output are in tokens; the context window covers input and output together. Rates are USD per 1 million tokens. A rate with a context-length range, such as (≤272k), changes when the input is above that range. The Usage tier column is the minimum usage tier (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/admin/rate-limits-usage-tiers.md) that can call the model.
[tab] Anthropic
anthropic/claude-fable-5, anthropic/claude-fable-5-1, and anthropic/claude-fable-5-2 are not available to organizations with zero data retention enabled.
[tab] OpenAI
openai/gpt-6.2-astra is not available to organizations with zero data retention enabled.
[tab] Google
The google/gemini-3.8-flash and google/gemini-3.7-flash rates apply through December 31, 2026.
[tab] xAI
xAI sets no separate output limit for xai/grok-4.7 and xai/grok-4.6, so max output equals the context window.
[tab] Z.AI
[tab] DeepSeek
[tab] Moonshot AI
Access by Usage Tier
Google, xAI, and open-weight models work at every usage tier. OpenAI models and most Anthropic models require Tier 1, which starts at $50 in cumulative credit purchases. anthropic/claude-opus-5, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, anthropic/claude-fable-5, anthropic/claude-fable-5-1, and anthropic/claude-fable-5-2 require Tier 2, which starts at $250. Check your tier under Usage tiers (https://console.perplexity.ai/project/pricing?tab=usage-tiers) on the API Console's Pricing page.
A request for a model above your tier returns HTTP 402. The message names your current tier and the model's minimum tier:
The check is on your tier, not on the type of credits you hold, so adding credits without reaching the model's minimum tier does not unlock it. Choose a model your current tier can use, or reach the required tier.
Organizations with zero data retention (ZDR) enabled cannot call anthropic/claude-fable-5, anthropic/claude-fable-5-1, anthropic/claude-fable-5-2, or openai/gpt-6.2-astra; those requests return HTTP 403. ZDR is off by default and requires a written agreement with Perplexity and account-level configuration; see Privacy & Security (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/resources/privacy-security.md). The FAQ (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/faq.md#access) lists the common 402 and 403 messages.
Billing
Usage is billed per token at the served model's rates in the tables, with no per-request fee. Orchestrator API usage draws on the same credit balance as the rest of the Perplexity API; see Pricing (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md) for how credits work. Project admins can review spend by model and by API key on the Billing page in the API Console. To keep environments or applications apart, use separate projects and API keys (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/projects.md).
* Cache reads are billed at the cache-read rate.
* Cache writes with the standard five-minute lifetime are billed once, at 1.25 times the input rate, on Anthropic models and on the openai/gpt-6.2-*, openai/gpt-6.1-*, openai/gpt-6-*, and openai/gpt-5.6-* models. One-hour cache writes, available on Anthropic models, are billed at 2 times the input rate.
* Reasoning tokens are billed at the output rate.
* service_tier on /chat/completions and /responses: a request served at the flex tier is billed at 0.5 times the token rates, and a request served at the priority tier at 2 times. Both values are accepted on OpenAI models only; other models return HTTP 400. openai/gpt-6.2-sol and openai/gpt-6.2-astra reject flex; send auto, default, or priority. auto and default are accepted on every model at the listed rates. On /messages, service_tier accepts only auto and standard_only, both at the listed rates.
Reasoning & Caching (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/reasoning-and-caching.md) explains how to turn on caching for each model family and where each format reports cached and reasoning tokens.
Other Models
Other models are available upon request and subject to approval. Contact api@perplexity.ai (mailto:api@perplexity.ai) to learn more.
List Models with the API
[accordion] Response
The response lists the models your usage tier can call, sorted by ID, with base token rates in USD per 1M tokens. It omits context windows, max output, and perplexity/auto. It does not apply zero data retention or organization model settings, so a ZDR organization whose tier includes them still sees the Claude Fable models and openai/gpt-6.2-astra. GET /orchestrator/v1/models/{model} returns one model; the ID contains a /, so the path is, for example, /orchestrator/v1/models/perplexity/kimi-k3.
A request for a model ID that is not in the catalog returns HTTP 404. /responses sets error.code to model_not_found and param to model. /messages returns its native envelope with error.type set to not_found_error. On /responses:
Next Steps
[card] Quickstart (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/quickstart.md)
Make your first Orchestrator API call.
[card] Reasoning & Caching (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/reasoning-and-caching.md)
Set reasoning effort and cache prompts in each request format.
[card] Routing & Reliability (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/orchestrator/routing-and-reliability.md)
Model routing with perplexity/auto, deployment selection, and failover.
[card] API Reference (https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/gateway-models-get.md)
List the models your usage tier can call.

https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/router/models.md: The response lists the models your usage tier can call, sorted by ID, with base token rates in USD per 1M tokens. It omits context windows, max output, and perplexity/auto. It does not apply zero data retention or organization model settings, so a ZDR organization whose tier includes them still sees the Claude Fable models and openai/gpt-6.2-astra. GET /orchestrator/v1/models/{model} returns one model; the ID contains a /, so the path is, for example, /orchestrator/v1/models/perplexity/kimi-k3.

https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/router/models.md: Usage is billed per token at the served model's rates in the tables, with no per-request fee. Orchestrator API usage draws on the same credit balance as the rest of the Perplexity API; see Pricing (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/pricing.md) for how credits work. Project admins can review spend by model and by API key on the Billing page in the API Console. To keep environments or applications apart, use separate projects and API keys (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/projects.md).
